text.p: Scottie Pippen does not sound happy about Dennis Rodman's trip to Las Vegas after another sub-par showing in the Chicago Bulls' Finals-tying loss to the Utah Jazz Sunday night.
"We don't have any control of what Dennis does off the court," Pippen said gravely. "It's his preference what he wants to do after the game.

"You would think that he would want to start to look and evaluate what's going on on the court with himself but as I stated it's his priority, and whatever he chooses to do, as a teammate I don't have any say-so about it."

Coach Phil Jackson said he had not "endorsed" Rodman's trip out of strait-laced Utah to the big "Sin City" in neighbouring Nevada. "I didn't endorse where he went. I thought maybe he was going to the state line. He made it beyond that," said Jackson.
Still, Jackson said, "Dennis is the kind of person that needs to blow off some steam and I imagine he got it done."
The coach added that Rodman returned for Monday's workouts in a timely fashion. "He was here early," Jackson said.
Teammate Steve Kerr had no concern about Rodman's trip. "No, I encourage that," he said with a laugh. "I think it's good for Dennis. He plays best when he does stuff like that."

Rodman himself, after getting no points and just six rebounds, made no apologies. "I went out and had a good time and was relaxing. I got rid of this bad taste in my mouth. I had to do that," said Rodman, who has won NBA titles with the Detroit Piston "Bad Boys" and last season's Bulls.

The flamboyant six-time rebounding champion added: "I'm not married. I don't have to entertain a family or nothing like that. So we have two days off (before Wednesday's Game 5) so I wanted to get the hell out of here and relax."
Rodman, who missed the last 13 games of the regular season with a knee strain, said he was still only about 80 percent physically.

"Sometimes you get in a little lull, or a funk, and it happens to be at the worst time. I got hurt at the wrong time of the season and it's haunting me right now. I just have to keep playing and hope I can get out of it right now," Rodman said.
